meeting_header: Date: 2027-09-14T15:00Z | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Nina Patel (Aperture VP Eng), Samir Gupta (Aperture Sr ML Eng), Leah Morris (Aperture Head of Platform), Tom Lee (Aperture Procurement)
summary: Quarterly health review focusing on usage trends, rising inference costs, recent latency spikes, and next steps to pilot Dedicated capacity. Customer wants clear SLA handoff and security artifacts before procurement commit.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run through Q3 usage, cost drivers, a quick incident recap, and then talk pilot and next steps. I'm Maya from Redwood.
[00:22] Nina Patel: Hi Maya, thanks. We have Leah and Samir here, Tom is joining from procurement. Ran into a couple of surprise bills last month so eager to get into detail.
[00:35] Diego Alvarez: quick intro, I'm Diego on the SE side, will show latency breakouts and configuration recommendations.
[00:50] Samir Gupta: Cool. High level we're seeing a 42% month-over-month increase in embedding calls and a 27% bump in chat generation.
[01:12] Priya Rao: FYI we've logged that growth against the pilot triggers - threshold hit for sales assist.
[01:30] Maya Chen: Ok, Samir can you give the traffic shape? burstiness, seq length?
[01:45] Samir Gupta: Mostly daytime ecom hours, 11am-2pm spike. Sequence lengths average 220 tokens for chat, embeddings are short ~512 dims calls but high volume. Some multimodal test calls too.
[02:10] Diego Alvarez: We ran sampling, P95 latency on hosted models drifted from 320ms to 620ms on the 09/04 spike; P99 occasionally hit 1.8s. Might be KV cache churn plus longer seqs.
[02:35] Nina Patel: 1.8 seconds is... not great for checkout flows. We saw cancellations.
[02:50] Samir Gupta: There was also an incident where a model fallback invoked, so some requests hit the smaller variant which increased tokens and latency — our prompts aren't always pinned.
[03:12] Maya Chen: That's where route pinning and rollout policies help — we can set canary and auto-fallback thresholds.
[03:30] Leah Morris: On the security side we need SOC 2 docs and confirmation of KMS integration. Procurement won't sign without it.
[03:48] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll attach SOC 2 + ISO artifacts. We support customer-managed KMS and HSM via our Private offering, and keywrap in Dedicated.
[04:05] Tom Lee: Any latency SLA for Dedicated? Our SREs want 99% under 350ms for gen endpoints.
[04:22] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated can give more predictable tail latencies; with autoscaling and reserved GPU pools you typically see P95 in the 200-400ms band depending on model and batching. We'll run a P50/P95 table by route.
[04:45] Nina Patel: Cost — we got a bill spike. Can you walk through the main drivers?
[05:02] Diego Alvarez: Sure, primary drivers are: token volume growth, quantization mismatch (we were serving FP16 variants when INT8 would be ok for embeddings), and low KV cache hit-rates causing more autoregressive tokens per request.
[05:25] Samir Gupta: Are there quick wins?
[05:32] Diego Alvarez: Yes: enable prefix caching for recurring sessions, use INT8 quant for large-batch embedding workloads, and adjust batching windows during off-peak to increase throughput.
[05:50] Maya Chen: We'll propose an Optimize plan that scores each endpoint for costing opportunities. Diego will run the detailed delta.
[06:05] Priya Rao: Also note we can do a short dedicated pilot with a burst window to validate SLA and cost — we usually do a 2-week pilot.
[06:20] Leah Morris: Network: VPC peering and private routes — do you support AWS PrivateLink?
[06:33] Maya Chen: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink on Private deployments; Dedicated customers can use a customer-managed VPC with peering and route controls. We'll include the network diagram.
[06:48] Samir Gupta: On cache churn, you mentioned KV cache eviction — is that on our side or Redwood's runtime?
[07:02] Diego Alvarez: Runtime side — we manage KV cache but customer can tune TTL/pinning. For chat-heavy workloads pinning the first n tokens reduces repeated compute.
[07:25] Nina Patel: For procurement, Tom needs the SLA in writing and a list of subprocessors.
[07:37] Tom Lee: Yes, and retention policies for logs and transcripts please.
[07:50] Maya Chen: We'll produce an SLA one-pager and list of subprocessors. Also retention policy options: default 30 days, enterprise-retain configurable.
[08:08] Diego Alvarez: Quick note on model variants: switching to a 4-bit quant for the gen model reduced cost 32% in our bench but added about +20ms in median latency. Tradeoff to discuss.
[08:31] Samir Gupta: 32% savings is big. Latency +20ms is fine for async chat, but not for our checkout path.
[08:45] Nina Patel: So separate routes for checkout and exploratory chat?
[08:52] Maya Chen: Exactly — route by SLO. Pin a low-latency variant for checkout, cheap quantized for analytics.
[09:07] Diego Alvarez: I'll include a suggested route map in the follow-up doc.
[09:18] Leah Morris: Are there any required infra changes for us to get Dedicated? We have limited on-prem networking windows.
[09:32] Priya Rao: For Dedicated we need a connectivity window to set up peering and access controls; usually 2-3 business days.
[09:45] Samir Gupta: On telemetry, can we get token-level breakdown by user cohort?
[09:55] Diego Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route token breakdown and you can tag tokens by key. We'll show an example export.
[10:12] Nina Patel: About pilot scope — what success metrics should we measure?
[10:22] Maya Chen: Proposed pilot KPIs: P95 latency for checkout routes < 400ms, cost per 1k tokens reduced by 20% vs hosted baseline, KV cache hit-rate > 85%, zero-severity incidents in pilot window.
[10:38] Nina Patel: That seems reasonable. Samir, can you sign off on instrumentation?
[10:45] Samir Gupta: Yes we'll add traces, and share a sample of user prompts.
[10:54] Maya Chen: Great. Quick incident recap — there was a 09/04 spike where an autoscaler misfired and we saw degraded tail. We rolled back a kernel patch.
[11:11] Diego Alvarez: transcription note: 'kernel patch' occasionally transcribed 'kernel batch' in some internal notes, so ignore that.
[11:25] Leah Morris: Any governance around evals/regression alerts? We run sensitive prompts.
[11:36] Priya Rao: Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set linked quality regressions; we can keep those results private to your org.
[11:48] Tom Lee: What about data residency? Some data must stay in EU.
[11:57] Maya Chen: We support region pinning; for Private deployments you can keep data entirely in your VPC region. We'll note options.
[12:15] Nina Patel: Okay let's walk through the proposed timeline.
[12:22] Diego Alvarez: Suggested: Week 0-1 prep (network, security review), Week 2 pilot deploy and smoke tests, Weeks 3-4 load validation, Week 5 pilot retrospective and SLA handoff.
[12:37] Samir Gupta: That fits our Q4 window, we want to make a procurement decision by end of Sep.
[12:46] Maya Chen: Procurement decision by end of Sep — tight but doable if we expedite docs.
[12:55] Leah Morris: We'll need a pricing anchor. Any estimate for a 2-week Dedicated pilot?
[13:05] Priya Rao: Typically pilots are discounted and billed monthly pro-rated; I'll put a pricing anchor in the follow-up.
[13:18] Nina Patel: On the billing spike — can you show us token-per-route billing?
[13:26] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll export a cost table and flag anomalous days.
[13:35] Samir Gupta: Also note we have a weekend bulk batch that fires nightly — that may have inflated embedding costs.
[13:45] Maya Chen: Good catch. We'll map batch windows and suggest moving heavy batch to off-peak or different quant profile.
[13:58] Tom Lee: SOC2 timeline — are you up-to-date?
[14:06] Maya Chen: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II in 2026 and maintain ISO 27001. We'll attach attestations and a redacted audit summary.
[14:18] Leah Morris: KMS integration specifics? we need rotation and key destruction details.
[14:28] Diego Alvarez: We support AWS KMS key wrapping and customer-provided keys for Private; rotation policy is configurable. We'll include a matrix.
[14:42] Samir Gupta: On the metric side, can you give a sample of the Console dashboard? we want to show engineering leadership.
[14:52] Priya Rao: We'll share a demo link and a short screen recording of the per-route dashboards.
[15:02] Nina Patel: Are there any lock-ins we should be aware of?
[15:09] Maya Chen: No vendor lock-in at the API level; models are standard open variants. Migration guidance is in the playbook.
[15:20] Samir Gupta: For the next call can Diego show the P50/P95 table and a cost delta for INT8 vs FP16?
[15:30] Diego Alvarez: Yes, will do.
[15:36] Maya Chen: Ok to recap next steps: Diego sends latency/cost tables, Maya sends security pack and SLA one-pager, Priya coordinates pilot kickoff scheduling.
[15:48] Nina Patel: Good. Any blockers?
[15:52] Leah Morris: Network peering window — need confirmation by Friday.
[15:58] Tom Lee: Procurement needs the SLA + subprocessors list to start legal review.
[16:05] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize those docs this week.
[16:15] Samir Gupta: I'll get the 7-day traffic sample and prompt mix.
[16:24] Priya Rao: I'll send a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and internal pre-call.
[16:33] Nina Patel: Sounds good. Thank you everyone.
[16:40] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up on the action items and keep the thread tight.
[16:48] (conference ends)
notes: Customer is near procurement decision; primary open items: SLA, SOC2 artifacts, network peering window.
Strong candidate for Dedicated pilot — clear runway for cost savings via quantization and caching.
Immediate risk: latency on checkout route; mitigations: route pinning + low-latency variant.
